positions.commentary: The host mentions that the guest, Drew Cohen, is known for making videos about Adobe, but the passage does not express a specific investment view on the company itself.
The host mentions that they want to talk about Uber in the context of AI updates and autonomous vehicles, but does not express a specific investment view.
DoorDash has slightly higher market share in a lot of areas compared to Uber.
Google aggregates a lot of restaurants and dominates search results for them, which could be relevant for food delivery.
Tesla might be picking off big cities similar to Waymo, which could be a headwind to profits.
Blackstone might fund 100,000 Waymos and become the fleet owner, which could adversely affect Uber's business.
The guest notes that Netflix is trading at a much higher valuation multiple (23-24 times) compared to the 16 times multiple he mentioned previously, implying it is more expensive.

thesis: This episode argues that Adobe faces significant existential risks from AI competition, with the speaker estimating that 20-50% of its business could disappear, while Uber is viewed as defensible but facing valuation risks and competitive headwinds from autonomous vehicle technology.

claims.claim: The speaker believes there is a strong case for Adobe to go wrong despite its growth.
claims.quote: But it does seem like there's a pretty strong case for a lot to go wrong. So, I think people are going to have to, I think people are going to land on one side of the fence here.

claims.claim: The business is defensible and will likely survive, but profitability faces risks from competition and promotions over the next few years.
claims.quote: So that to me is a more defensible business. Having said that, you know, DoorDash and a lot of areas does have slightly higher market share but it still seems like a better business

claims.claim: Uber has an uncertain future, and the market is re-rating its valuation, trading at 20 times forward earnings and 32 times trailing.
claims.quote: I think Uber has a pretty uncertain future at this point and the market is trying to re-rate that to some extent. What kind of valuation are we looking at after this re-rating? Yeah, so it's trading at like 20 times forward earnings at this point right now, 32 times trailing

claims.claim: Uber will be fine in the long run, but investors need to decide if the current valuation is acceptable given the risks.
claims.quote: But I don't know, I guess if you're asking me base case scenario I think they'll be fine. Drew, you know, I have to say you but a little more optimistic these days than you were historically.

claims.claim: Uber will likely survive over a 10-year horizon, but margins are up for debate and the stock may be overvalued.
claims.quote: You know, what their margins are gonna be I do think is up for debate though. Yeah, I guess so your use of the word Uber's gonna be okay as a broad interpretation is Uber gonna be teetering on the edge of bankruptcy is Uber going to be, you know, just hanging in there okay, broad definition.

claims.claim: DoorDash has slightly higher market share in a lot of areas compared to Uber.
claims.quote: Having said that, you know, DoorDash and a lot of areas does have slightly higher market share but it still seems like a better business

claims.claim: Adobe has an uncertain future and is trading at 10 times earnings, raising questions about whether investors are properly compensated for that risk.
claims.quote: You know, Adobe has this very uncertain future and you know, they're at 10 times earning so an investor can say, okay, well, I'm taking this uncertain future but am I being compensated properly for it?

claims.claim: Google aggregates a lot of restaurants and dominates search results for them, which could be relevant for food delivery.
claims.quote: And so it is interesting though because you know who else has a lot of restaurants on aggregated together and knows about them is Google, right? You could search any restaurant you want and the first thing that's gonna come up is the Google business page.

claims.claim: Waymo could place cars in some cities with enough density to cause Uber to lose market share, but the longer time frame for autonomous vehicles is uncertain.
claims.quote: My broader argument here is that it will be easier for Waymo to place cars in some cities and with some level of density that Uber does lose market share or has to compete to some extent greater than they have been. I do think the longer time frame on the whole autonomous vehicle is longer.

claims.claim: Tesla might be picking off big cities similar to Waymo, which could be a headwind to profits.
claims.quote: One is that it still is relatively concentrated profits in the biggest cities, you know, 25% of profits in the top US cities and I would expect similar concentration internationally. So if Waymo is just picking off those big cities and maybe Tesla is doing the same, that could be enough to be a good headwind to profits.

claims.claim: Blackstone might fund 100,000 Waymos and become the fleet owner, which could adversely affect Uber's business.
claims.quote: maybe teams up with a private equity firm like Blackstone and funds 100,000 waymos and now they're gonna be the fleet owner and I don't know that I would really feel that confident that that can't happen and that that it's not gonna have an adverse effect on Uber's business.

claims.claim: The speaker feels Adobe is like a melting ice cube and finds the narrative that it is a steady business hard to believe.
claims.quote: And it's just Adobe's kind of reminiscent of a melting ice cube to me, and I can't get over it. And again, that's just me on a 10,000-stand-foot view watching your videos on 3X speed. I can't get over that narrative.

claims.claim: The speaker believes Adobe is in the 'too hard pile' and finds it challenging to see them maintaining what they've maintained.
claims.quote: It just feels, to me, it feels like it's in the too hard pile. Maybe Adobe withstands, and maybe that's how you look at it. But if I'm looking at a real easy use case of AI, it feels like Adobe's one of these software companies, I have a more challenging time seeing them maintaining what they've maintained at this point.

claims.claim: The speaker thinks the competition is different this time and buys the idea that AI is creating different images while Adobe is just an image modifier.
